sources.citation: Held checks for the successor languages: (Usun Apau/Mainstream Kenyah [xkl]) and baku1265/, umal1238/ (Uma' Lung [ulu]).
sources.note: main1275 check holds a Google Books snippet of Burkhardt 2006 'The Lepu' Aga' vowel system' (Reflections in Borneo Rivers, pp. 35-63): 'In Lepu Aga', stresss [sic] falls on the nucleus of the penult if it contains any other vowel but schwa. In case schwa occupies this position, stress shifts to the ultima' (page not visible) -- Upper Baram (Sarawak) Highland Kenyah, not a Mahakam variety. umal1238 check: Blust 2007 Oma Longh historical phonology (OL 46) paywalled/unread. Nothing in these folders concerns 'Mahakam Kenyah' as such.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-245: rename [xkl] Kenyah Kelinyau to Mainstream Kenyah and merge Madang [mqd] and Bakung [boc] into it.
ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-246: create [ulu] Uma' Lung.
sources.note: Nothing; identity only (Uma' Lung 'stands out among the other mainstream' Kenyah varieties per Soriente 2006).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request Number 2007-264: retire [xkm] Kenyah, Mahakam as non-existent (submitted by Karl Anderbeck, SIL Indonesia Branch, 2007-08-31; adopted 2008-01-14). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Identity document only: 'Kenyah, Mahakam is a vague name associated mainly to toponym or ethnonym of some Kenyah groups' (p.2); the name came from Wurm & Hattori (1981); RA comment: retired as non-existent because it is unclear whether the speakers belong to Mainstream Kenyah [xkl] (request 2007-245) or Uma' Lung [ulu] (request 2007-246). Sources named: Soriente 2003 UKM PhD, Soriente 2005 paper, Soriente 2006 Mencaleny (p.4).
